title: Gift App Setup Deck
project: giving my gift to the world (public gift swipe app, Machan's second post on X)
example_data: All app screens are rendered HTML mockups with made-up SAMPLE data (recipient "Robin", .example stores).

pairs.ask: How should people answer the setup questions?

optionA.label: Tap chips
optionA.desc: Every answer is a row of chips. One tap, done. Fast on a phone.
optionA.more: Chips work for age bands, relationship, occasion and interests alike, so the whole setup feels like one pattern. Great for people in a hurry.

optionB.label: Slide to answer
optionB.desc: Sliders for anything with a range: age, budget, how practical vs. playful.
optionB.more: Sliders feel more playful and let people say "somewhere between". They need a clear live value so it never feels vague.

pairs.ask: One question at a time, or all on one page?

optionA.label: One per screen
optionA.desc: A card per question with a big Next. Feels like a deck already.
optionA.more: Easy to focus, easy to go back. The step bar shows how close the swiping is.

optionB.label: One scrolling page
optionB.desc: All the questions on one page, long ones folded down until tapped.
optionB.more: People see everything up front and can jump around. Fold-downs keep it short on a phone.

pairs.ask: How does someone set the budget?

optionA.label: Price chips
optionA.desc: A few ready ranges. Tap one, move on.
optionA.more: Fastest option and works well in any currency. A small "custom" chip covers everyone else.

optionB.label: Range slider
optionB.desc: Drag two handles to set a low and a high. Live price above.
optionB.more: Precise and satisfying to drag. Snaps to $5 steps so it never lands on odd numbers.

optionA.label: Soft: "around $75"
optionA.desc: One number. A few gifts a little over can sneak in, marked clearly.
optionA.more: Friendlier and finds more good ideas. Anything over the number gets a small "+$9" tag so there are no surprises.

optionB.label: Hard cap: "up to $75"
optionB.desc: Never shows anything over the cap. A check mark says in budget.
optionB.more: Clear and trustworthy for people on a tight budget. Fewer ideas near the top of the range.

pairs.ask: How do people pick what the person is into?

optionA.label: Picture tiles
optionA.desc: A grid of tiles with small pictures. Tap all that fit.
optionA.more: Visual and quick to scan. Twelve tiles on screen, "more" for the rest.

optionB.label: Type and tag
optionB.desc: A search box that suggests tags as you type, plus popular ones below.
optionB.more: Handles anything, even niche hobbies. Better for people who know exactly what their person loves.

pairs.ask: Just pick interests, or swipe them too?

optionA.label: Pick a few
optionA.desc: Tap up to five. Simple, quick, the swiping starts after.
optionA.more: Keeps setup short so the gift swiping is the fun part.

optionB.label: Swipe interests
optionB.desc: Interests come as quick yes / no cards. Setup already feels like the app.
optionB.more: A tiny warm-up deck: right for "into it", left for "not really". It teaches the swipe before gifts arrive.

optionA.label: Quick: four questions
optionA.desc: Who, age, budget, interests. Under a minute, then straight to swiping.
optionA.more: Fast for a public app where people try it on a whim. Relationship and occasion are guessed as "general" unless added.

optionB.label: Full: eight, with skips
optionB.desc: Adds relationship, occasion, vibe and "avoid". Every extra can be skipped.
optionB.more: Sharper gift pairs in Round 1. A "skip the rest" link keeps it from feeling long.

pairs.ask: How do we learn who they are to you, and why now?

optionA.label: Tap the cards
optionA.desc: Two quick card choices: who they are, what it is for.
optionA.more: Clear, structured answers that shape the gift pairs well.

optionB.label: Tell me in a sentence
optionB.desc: One free-text line. Machan reads it and fills in the rest.
optionB.more: Feels personal and fast. Machan shows what he understood as chips so people can fix it.

optionA.label: Warm and personal
optionA.desc: "What lights them up?" Questions that feel like a friend asking.
optionA.more: Matches the gift mood and Machan's voice. A touch longer to read.

optionB.label: Crisp and quick
optionB.desc: "Interests." Short labels, no chatter, straight to the point.
optionB.more: Feels efficient and modern. Less charm, faster for repeat visitors.

optionA.label: Recap card first
optionA.desc: "Here is who we are shopping for." Edit anything, then start.
optionA.more: A last check builds trust in the picks. One extra tap.

optionB.label: Straight in, shuffle moment
optionB.desc: A short moment with Machan shuffling cards, then the first pair.
optionB.more: Keeps momentum. The shuffle doubles as the loading screen while pairs are made.
